tts: Why do rival gas stations always end up right next to each other?
Sharing customers sounds like terrible business.
One road. Drivers spread evenly. Everyone fills up at the closest station.
Pip sets up at one end. Dot at the other. Half the road each.
caps: Pip sets up at one end.

tts: Pip slides toward the middle. Everyone behind still comes to Pip, plus a chunk of Dot's drivers.
caps: plus a chunk of Dot's drivers.

tts: So Dot slides in too, and steals them back.
Move, counter move, until they're back to back in the center.
And now they're stuck. Whoever steps away hands the other a bigger share.
This is Hotelling's Law, first described in 1929.
The twist? Drivers at the ends now drive farther. Two stations at the quarter marks would split customers just the same, and serve everyone better.
Real towns add other reasons, like busy corners. But this pull shows up everywhere. Coffee shops. Even politicians chasing the middle.
Everything is a game. These are the hidden moves.
